claim: Metacognitive sensitivity (confidence separating right from wrong) is a different quantity from calibration (bias), and raw discrimination depends on task difficulty; efficiency (meta-d'/d') or matched-difficulty comparison is needed.
agent_test: Report AUROC and ECE separately for the agent's confidence, binned by task difficulty.
audit_note: Fleming & Lau (listed 3x, one paper) says sensitivity scales with task performance and favours meta-d'/d'; Rahnev & Fleming is a shared-author follow-up; Steyvers link not opened.

claim: In humans, introspective accuracy is a stable individual trait (split-half r=0.69) that is dissociable from task accuracy (r=-0.11, N=32) and linked to anterior prefrontal grey matter (peak t=4.8, corrected). GAP UPDATE: lesion work (n=7) shows a domain-specific deficit; an N=308 fMRI study shows a prefrontal link but as an activation decrease; no direct large-N volume replication found.
agent_test: No direct agent test; human background only.

claim: Metacognitive efficiency shows partial domain generality in humans (5 of 6 cross-task correlations significant, N=181) but estimates move with procedure (all-contrast vs 1-contrast AUC +0.034, d=0.57).
agent_test: When testing the agent, measure confidence quality per task type, not one global score.
audit_note: Mazancieux et al. (N=181, 5 of 6 cross-task correlations, via 95% HDI) and Rahnev & Fleming (type 2 AUC difference 0.034, d=0.57) match.

claim: Verbalized confidence from a vanilla prompt discriminates weakly: GPT-4 mean AUROC 62.7% (chance 50%); weaker models average ECE above 0.377; confidences cluster at 80-100%.
agent_test: Ask the agent to state confidence on a held-out set; compute AUROC against correctness at equal tokens.

claim: Low ECE can hide zero discrimination: GPT-4 on GSM8K (93.6% accuracy) gets ECE 0.064 by saying 100% every time.
agent_test: Always pair ECE with AUROC; flag constant-confidence outputs.

claim: Agreement across several sampled answers predicts correctness far better than a single verbalized number: GSM8K AUROC 54.8% (Top-K, M=1) to 92.7% (M=5 consistency, GPT-3.5); semantic entropy AUROC 0.83 TriviaQA, 0.77 CoQA vs distinct-answer count 0.79, 0.66. GAP UPDATE 2026: for reasoning models (Del 2026) self-consistency lags verbalized confidence at equal samples (SC@2 math 70.5 vs VC@2 73.5), though in small open models SC (0.82) beats VC (0.67). The ordering depends on model class.
agent_test: Compare self-report vs agreement-of-k-samples as an abstain/escalate trigger at equal total tokens.

claim: Gains from more samples saturate (M=1 to 13) and self-consistency raises accuracy: Wang +17.9% GSM8K best model, LaMDA-137B 17.1 to 27.7; imperfect prompt 17.1 to 14.9 recovered by sampling; on GSM8K SC 82.5/85.3/88.2 at 3/6/9 samples.
agent_test: Plot accuracy vs k at fixed token budget; find knee.
audit_note: Wang (17.9 abs, LaMDA 17.1->27.7, flawed prompts 17.1->14.9 then 23.4 with 40 paths), Huang Table 7 (82.5/85.3/88.2 at 3/6/9 responses) and Xiong (M=1..13 saturates) all match; Wang is listed 3x as one paper and the 82.5/85.3/88.2 figures come from Huang, not Wang.

claim: Confidence-weighted voting cuts cost: CISC needs over 40% fewer paths; P(True) SC needs 18.6 samples to match CISC at 10 (46% saving); Adaptive-Consistency cuts samples up to 7.9x with under 0.1% accuracy loss; DeepConf reaches 99.9% on AIME 2025 (GPT-OSS-120B, offline) vs 97.0% majority, and separately its online mode cuts tokens up to 84.7% (at 97.9% accuracy).
agent_test: Implement early stopping on agreement or confidence-weighted votes; measure tokens saved at equal accuracy.
audit_note: DeepConf 99.9% (offline, tail confidence, 10% retention) and the 84.7% token cut (online DeepConf-low, 97.9% accuracy) are different settings, so the sentence implies both gains come together; CISC, P(True) and Adaptive-Consistency numbers match.
claim_before_audit: Confidence-weighted voting cuts cost: CISC needs over 40% fewer paths; P(True) SC needs 18.6 samples to match CISC at 10 (46% saving); Adaptive-Consistency cuts samples up to 7.9x with under 0.1% accuracy loss; DeepConf reaches 99.9% on AIME 2025 (GPT-OSS-120B) vs 97.0% majority, up to 84.7% fewer tokens.

claim: Asking models for a probability that their own answer is true works for large models with the right format: P(True)>0.5 filtering raises accuracy on all five tasks (up to 52B); calibration improves with few-shot and with showing own samples; 52B P(IK) AUROC 0.864 to 0.928 on some tasks but as low as 0.606 on one.
agent_test: Use P(True) on the agent's own candidate as one weak signal; check AUROC on our tasks.

claim: Verbalized confidence beats token probabilities for RLHF models on some sets (gpt-3.5-turbo SciQ ECE 0.256 to 0.065; TriviaQA AUC 0.869 to 0.896) but not on adversarial ones (TruthfulQA AUC 0.418 below chance, verbalized 0.455-0.55).
agent_test: Test verbalized vs sampling confidence on adversarial/misleading items.

claim: Models trained to express uncertainty can generalise: finetuned verbalized numbers beat a constant baseline out of distribution (Multi-answer MSE 22.0 vs 34.1; zero-shot answer logit 37.4); a thousand graded examples suffice for finetuned calibration (Kapoor et al. 2024), and prompting alone is insufficient.
agent_test: Not testable without training; instead keep a per-task-type calibration table from agent history.
audit_note: Lin et al. Multi-answer MSE: finetuned verbalized numbers 22.0, constant baseline 34.1; 37.4 is the zero-shot answer-logit baseline. The 1,000-example claim is Kapoor et al., not Lin et al.
claim_before_audit: Models trained to express uncertainty can generalise: finetuned verbalized numbers beat a constant baseline out of distribution (Multi-answer MSE 22.0 vs 37.4); a thousand graded examples suffice for finetuned calibration, and prompting alone lags even at stronger base models.

claim: Chain of thought alone does not give better discrimination (confidences stay 80-100%); reasoning models that revise inside the chain become better calibrated and discriminate better (TriviaQA ECE 0.042 vs 0.150 without CoT; NonambigQA AUROC 0.749 vs 0.618).
agent_test: Compare confidence AUROC at end vs mid-chain for the agent; cut at equal tokens.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without external feedback fails to help and often hurts: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 to 41.8; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0; and sampling beat debate at equal budget. GAP UPDATE 2026: newer models gain from intrinsic revision when the task has checkable constraints (SAT, 65.7% of errors removed) but flip correct answers up to 13.25% on open reasoning (BBEH, HLE).
schema_part: G (no self-revise on self-report); O (revise only with external evidence)
agent_test: Run revise-with-no-new-evidence vs sample-and-vote at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs show confirmation-like bias: change-of-mind rate 32.5% when own answer hidden vs 13.1% when shown; opposing advice overweighted vs supporting (85.0% vs 39.2% change).
agent_test: Hide the earlier answer during review; compare error rate at equal tokens.

claim: Confident-sounding LLM text misleads people: human AUC 0.59-0.60 vs model AUC 0.75-0.78; explanation length inflates confidence; matching explanation tone to model confidence narrows the gap. Alignment data penalises expressions of doubt; 47% error rate among confident responses.
agent_test: Check whether the agent's final answer style tracks its measured uncertainty.
audit_note: Steyvers et al. (AUC humans 0.589-0.602 vs model 0.746-0.781, length effect, tone matching) and Zhou et al. (humans biased against uncertainty in alignment data; 47% error among confident responses when prompted) match; Steyvers listed 3x as one paper; Yona et al. gives no number.

claim: LLM self-knowledge is real but narrow: self-prediction beats cross-prediction (Llama-3-70B 48.5% vs GPT-4o 31.8%, +17 points); introspective awareness works in about 20% of trials with 0 false positives in production models; fails on long outputs.
schema_part: G (no trust in introspection of long solutions)
agent_test: Test whether the agent can predict its own success on short vs long tasks better than a different model.

claim: Radical-belief holders show lower metacognitive sensitivity and smaller confidence updates on disconfirming evidence (replicated in N=344, 381, 417).
agent_test: Score agent confidence change after contrary evidence is introduced.

claim: Confidence can be read as a Bayesian probability or from own action as evidence (Fleming and Daw 2017; Kiani and Shadlen 2009, 70 LIP neurons) giving a theory for why confidence tracks accuracy.
agent_test: Theory only.
audit_note: Fleming & Daw 2017 treat confidence as Bayesian probability correct and own action as evidence; Kiani & Shadlen 2009 figure caption cites 70 LIP neurons (from PubMed record); the 'own action' idea belongs to Fleming & Daw only.

claim: For frontier reasoning models, one end-of-chain verbalized confidence discriminates moderately (AUROC 78.8 math, 73.8 STEM, 68.5 humanities at K=1) and a hybrid of verbalized confidence plus two-sample agreement adds up to +12 AUROC; gains past about K=5 are small outside math.
agent_test: Measure AUROC of end-of-chain confidence, agreement, and the combination on 100 held-out items per domain.

claim: Reasoning models stay overconfident: confidence on wrong answers is often above 85%, and more reasoning effort raises overconfidence on wrong answers (o3-Mini ECE +7 points low to high effort); a self-review pass helps some models and hurts others.
agent_test: Test the agent's confidence at low and high thinking effort on items it gets wrong.

claim: Confidence quality varies by domain inside each model (33-model atlas: Applied/Professional AUROC .742 vs Formal Reasoning .658, Natural Science .652) and cell estimates are noisy (median CI width .199), so a per-type calibration table must be coarse and refitted per model.
agent_test: Build the table on 4 task types; check split-half stability before using.

claim: Self-estimated success of coding agents is near chance and overconfident (true 22-35%, predicted up to 77%; AUROC 0.51-0.64, CIs include 0.5); an execution check is the only strong gate (functional clustering: returned-answer error 65% to 2%).
schema_part: G (no self-report as evidence); O (run external check)
agent_test: Use test results, not model confidence, to decide to revise or accept.

claim: Reviewing a finished solution anchors the reviewer on plausibility; bug-finding framing cuts overconfident-failure rate from 72% to 45% and lifts Claude AUROC 0.55 to 0.64. Direct evidence that hiding the model's own earlier answer helps remains absent beyond Kumaran 2025.
agent_test: A/B: review with and without the earlier answer visible, plus bug-finding framing; same items, count error rates.

claim: Confidence-guided early stopping saves about 58% of calls at equal accuracy (CGES) but the evaluated variants need token probabilities or a reward model; with no logprobs only answer-count stopping or a verbalized scalar remain, and the loss for verbalized scalars is untested.
agent_test: Try answer-count stopping on the API and measure accuracy loss against fixed K.

claim: Wording and hedges do not track internal uncertainty (cMFG 0.52-0.57 vs 0.5 chance baseline for 5 models) and models do not abstain even when penalties make it optimal; stated confidence must be read by the scaffold and the threshold set outside the model.
agent_test: Apply an external threshold to measured agreement, not to the model's own abstain decision.

claim: For long outputs, confidence ranking collapses at atomic-claim resolution but is usable at line level (SALT, 50+ LLMs); claim-level semantic entropy variants (SeSE) beat entropy baselines in long-form factual text, but no tested method addresses multi-step agent trajectories (TrACE is the only per-step test, 3B model, n=30-50).
agent_test: Score confidence per step or per line and test whether the first low-confidence step predicts the failure.

claim: Internal states know more than stated confidence: a probe reaches AUROC 0.95 vs verbalized 0.67 (open models), and 65% of wrong traces show high stated confidence with high internal error score; the signal is diagnostic and could not be used to repair errors.
agent_test: Not available to a black-box agent; use sample agreement as the substitute.
